artists.biography:
The Damned are an English rock band formed in London in 1976. They were the first punk rock band from the United Kingdom to release a single ("New Rose"), an album (Damned Damned Damned), to have a record on the UK music charts, and to tour the United States. The Damned later evolved into one of the forerunners of the gothic genre.
They have incorporated numerous styles into their music and image, including: garage rock, psychedelic rock, cabaret, and the theatrical rock of Screaming Lord Sutch and Alex Harvey. Lead singer Dave Vanian's vocal style has been described as similar to a crooner. The Damned have dissolved and reformed many times, with Vanian as the sole constant member; the lineups have always included either guitarist Captain Sensible and/or drummer Rat Scabies, who are both founding members. The current line-up is Vanian, Captain Sensible, Monty Oxy Moron, Pinch and Stu West.

perplexity.description:
Released in November 1979 by Chiswick Records, Machine Gun Etiquette is the third studio album by the English punk rock band The Damned. Marking the first record with their reformed lineup—Dave Vanian (vocals), Captain Sensible (guitar), Rat Scabies (drums), and Algy Ward (bass)—the album signaled a revitalized era for the band. Musically, Machine Gun Etiquette blends raw punk energy with melodic hooks and new wave influences, showcasing the group’s evolving sound. The album features a mix of original tracks, covers (including the MC5’s “Looking at You”), and standout singles like “Love Song,” “Smash It Up,” and “I Just Can’t Be Happy Today,” which helped solidify The Damned’s reputation for both aggression and accessibility.

In the context of The Damned’s discography, Machine Gun Etiquette stands as a pivotal release, bridging their early punk roots with a more refined and diverse approach. It was the first album following their breakup and reunion, and many fans regard it as the start of their most creative period. The album reached No. 31 on the UK Albums Chart and received critical acclaim for its energy, songwriting, and production. Over time, it has been recognized as one of the band’s finest works, earning a silver certification and enduring praise as a classic of the late 1970s British punk and new wave scene.
